'''Phaltan''' ({{audio|Phaltan.ogg|pronunciation}}) is a city, [[tehsil]] and [[municipal council]] in the [[Satara district]] in the [[States and union territories of India|Indian state]] of [[Maharashtra]]. The city is about {{convert|59|km|mi|0}} northeast of the city of [[Satara (city)|Satara]] and about 110 km from [[Pune]].

== History ==
{{Main|Phaltan State}}
Phaltan was one of the non-salute Maratha [[princely states]] of British India, under the central division of the [[Bombay presidency]]. It measured 397 square miles (1,028 km<sup>2</sup>) in area. According to the 1901 census, the population decreased by 31% to 45,739; the town's population was 9,512. In 1901, the state had revenue estimated at £13,000, and paid a tribute of £640 to the British Raj.{{cn|date=July 2026}}

== Geography ==
Phaltan has an average elevation of 568 meters (1,863 feet).

Phaltan's climate is an inland climate of Maharashtra. The temperature ranges from {{convert|15|to|45|°C|F|0}}.<ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/publication/237381447_Long_term_weather_trends_in_western_Maharashtra Long term weather trends in western Maharashtra]</ref> Summer in Phaltan is comparatively hot and dry when compared to neighboring inland cities. Maximum temperatures exceed {{convert|40|°C|F|0}} every summer and typically range between {{convert|38|-|45|°C|F}}. Lows during this season are around {{convert|25|-|28|°C|F}}.

The city receives less rainfall from June to September, and it has been declared as a drought-prone place by the government. Phaltan sometimes does not get rainfall during the rainy season.

Winter starts in Phaltan from November to February. The winter temperatures are significantly higher compared to other cities in Maharashtra such as [[Pune]] and [[Nasik|Nashik]]. Lowest temperatures range from {{convert|14|-|16|°C|F}}, while highests are in the range of {{convert|29|-|32|°C|F}}. Humidity is low in this season.

Phaltan crosses a drought-prone area; a dry area is present to the south and south-west of Phaltan, a dry area begins. Water for drinking and irrigation is provided by the Veer Dam on the Nira river.

== Demographics ==
According to the [[2001 Census of India]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.censusindia.net/results/town.php?stad=A&state5=999|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040616075334/http://www.censusindia.net/results/town.php?stad=A&state5=999|archive-date=2004-06-16|title= Census of India 2001: Data from the 2001 Census, including cities, villages and towns  (Provisional)|access-date=2008-11-01|publisher= Census Commission of India}}</ref> Phaltan had a population of 60,172. Males constituted 51% of the population and females 49%. Phaltan has an average literacy rate of 75%, higher than the national average of 59.5%: male literacy is 80%, and female literacy is 70%. In Phaltan, 12% of the population was under six years of age.

== Culture ==

Phaltan is the birthplace of Chakrapani Prabhu, whom the followers of [[Mahanubhava]] Sampradaya consider an [[avatar]] among the 5 Krishnas.<ref name="Bhusari">R. M. Bhusari, Prachin Maharashtracha Dharmik Itihas (प्राचीन महाराष्ट्राचा धार्मिक इतिहास),  Marathi Sahitya Parishad, Hyderabad, 1966, p. 136</ref>

==Villages==
[[File:Bhilkati.jpg|thumb|right|Bhilkati]]
Villages in the tehsil include:
*Bhilkati ({{coord|18|1|10|N|74|22|26|E|display=inline}}), where the main activity of the community is [[farming]].
*[[Girvi]] is a village located at southeast of phaltan.It is at the base of varugad fort.

== Industry ==
[[File:Shriram sahkari sakhar karkhana.jpg|thumb|Cummins manufacturing plant]]
As a tehsil, Phaltan has two sugar factories: New Phaltan Sugar Works Ltd., [[Sakharwadi]] and Shri Ram Sahakari Sakhar Karkhana Pvt. Ltd., Phaltan.<ref>[http://www.mahasugarfed.org/images/pdf/pvt_sugar_fact.pdf sugar]</ref>

Cummins India Ltd. has its 300-acre "mega-site" plant in Phaltan, which is being used to manufacture engines.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Agtey Athale |first1=Gouri |title=Cummins India to make Phaltan a true megasite |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/cummins-india-to-make-phaltan-a-true-megasite/articleshow/9271861.cms |access-date=10 May 2020 |work=The Economic Times |date=18 July 2011}}</ref>
[[File:Phaltan M I D C Surawadi (Cummins).JPG|thumb|Cummins India Ltd. in Phaltan [[Maharashtra Industrial Development Corporation|MIDC]]]]

== Education ==
The [[Nimbkar Agricultural Research Institute]] is located in Phaltan. It focuses on agriculture, renewable energy, animal husbandry and sustainable development. Its work on energy self-sufficient tehsils (which became a national policy) was based on the extensive research on biomass availability in Phaltan Taluka.<ref>[https://www.currentscience.ac.in/Downloads/article_id_082_06_0632_0637_0.pdf Taluka's can provide critical mass for sustainable development of India]</ref><ref>[http://www.epw.in/journal/1995/51/special-articles/energy-self-sufficient-talukas-solution-national-energy-crisis.html Energy Self Sufficient Talukas - A solution to National Energy Crisis; EPW, Vol. 30, Issue No. 51, 23 Dec, 1995]</ref>

== In popular culture ==

Phaltan is best known as the geospatial basis for the contemporary storyline of the 2010 [[Priyadarshan]] film ''[[Khatta Meetha (2010 film)|Khatta Meetha]]'' in which [[Akshay Kumar]]'s character Sachin Tichkule is a local native of the town, with the Tichkule family shown to be descendants of the village's royal family.
